title: Dawn Without Arrival
intent: A restrained late-night jazz quintet gradually shifts from shadowed minor toward softened, unresolved brightness, offering relaxation through spacious phrasing and gentle repetition.

tempo.feel: Slow, floating swing with spacious phrasing; increasingly sparse near the ending.

tonality.mode: minor with relative-major inflections and common-tone ambiguity

instrumentation.name: Piano
instrumentation.role: States and develops the simple central motif; provides spacious harmonic voicings.
instrumentation.timbre: Warm, intimate acoustic tone with restrained attack and occasional upper-register resonance.

instrumentation.name: Upright bass
instrumentation.role: Creates a barely moving low-register foundation and supports the harmonic transformation.
instrumentation.timbre: Soft, rounded pizzicato with occasional sustained notes.

instrumentation.name: Brush kit
instrumentation.role: Maintains a subtle floating pulse without a pronounced backbeat.
instrumentation.timbre: Whispered brushes, featherlight cymbal shimmer, low dynamic ceiling.

instrumentation.name: Flugelhorn
instrumentation.role: Lengthens and gently transforms the piano motif into the emotional foreground.

instrumentation.name: Vibraphone
instrumentation.role: Adds a late luminous halo around the returning motif and final harmony.
instrumentation.timbre: Sparse, softly damped notes with delicate sustained shimmer.

structure.direction: Solo piano presents a simple, shadowed motif in minor-ninth and suspended colors, with generous silence.
Upright bass and whispered brushes enter with a barely moving floating swing; piano broadens its voicings while preserving the motif.
Flugelhorn enters in long, breath-like phrases, gradually introducing relative-major inflections without resolving the underlying ambiguity.
Vibraphone adds sparse, glowing tones around the flugelhorn and piano; density increases gently but never becomes dramatic.
Layers recede in reverse order, leaving piano, bass, and a final shared common tone that fades without a full cadence.

production: Intimate acoustic room with warm, soft-edged recording, close piano and bass perspective, restrained stereo width, gentle natural reverb, clear separation, and preserved dynamic nuance. Avoid abrupt transitions; let entrances and exits feel breathed and deliberate.
assumptions: D minor is used as a flexible tonal center for the shadowed opening.
A slow 58 BPM pulse supports the requested floating swing and relaxation.
lyriaPrompt: Late-night noir jazz quintet for relaxation, approximately 3 minutes, slow floating swing at 58 BPM in 4/4. Instrumental only, no vocals. Begin with intimate piano stating a simple motif in shadowed minor-ninth and suspended harmony, leaving generous silence. Gradually add soft upright bass and whispering brushes with a barely moving pulse. Let breathy flugelhorn lengthen and gently transform the motif, introducing subtle relative-major inflections while preserving unresolved common-tone ambiguity. Near the later section, add sparse, softly shimmering vibraphone as a luminous halo. Keep dynamics restrained, phrasing spacious, and the acoustic room warm and intimate. Recede by removing vibraphone, flugelhorn, brushes, and bass in turn, ending on a quiet shared common tone without a full cadence. Avoid abrupt drops, flashy virtuosity, harsh brightness, pronounced backbeat, cinematic bombast, and vocals.
